text:
emily: noticed something weird on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate — p50 moved down ~15ms, p95 unchanged, but p99 actually improved after the routing policy tweak this morning. did anyone dig in? :thinking:

devon: I saw that too when I was eyeballing rollout metrics. looks like client cohort A got routed to the new fast-path pool, others stayed on old pool. could be a cohort split artifact.

sam: can you paste the endpoint + time range? want to check sample counts. sometimes low-sample p99 jumps around.

emily: sure — observed between 08:12–09:10 UTC. dashboard link: https://console/redwood/dashboards/endpoint-latency#/v1/generate (will share screenshot in thread). p50 drop ~15ms, p95 ~same, p99 -8ms. total requests ~18k in window.

anjali: odd. if new pool has slightly faster median but fewer tail-reducing resources (e.g., smaller batch sizes), that could compress p50 but leave p95. p99 improving suggests tail-specific changes though. did the routing policy change include cache affinity or regional pinning?

devon: routing change was: prefer pool-fast if client tag in [cohort-A] or token_count < 128. also we enabled aggressive prefix KV cache for that pool (cache TTL 30s).

emily: ohhh cache TTL — that explains p50 improvement (more cache hits) but why p99 improves too? cache sometimes removes expensive token ops so tail might shrink. but sample distribution by client matters.

sam: quick hypothesis: cohort-A is high-QPS mobile clients with many short requests. moving them to fast-path increases short-request weight => p50 shifts down overall. but p99 improves because offloaded long-running large-token requests to a different pool with better tail latency (maybe different GPU type or lower co-tenancy).

nora: I can run a console query for percentiles by client_tag and token_count buckets. want p50/p95/p99 for each (08:00-09:30 UTC). give me 10m.

emily: please. also include sample counts and the routing.pool tag in the breakdown.

nora: running now — here's the query I used:
```sql
SELECT client_tag, routing_pool, token_bucket, pct(50), pct(95), pct(99), count(*)
FROM latency_events
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-21T08:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-21T09:30:00Z'
GROUP BY client_tag, routing_pool, token_bucket
```

nora: results (summary): cohort-A on pool-fast: p50 72ms, p95 210ms, p99 320ms, cnt 9.2k. cohort-B on pool-old: p50 88ms, p95 215ms, p99 550ms, cnt 7.8k. large-token bucket (>512): mostly on pool-old, p99 1.1s, cnt 1.1k.

anjali: that matches sam's hypothesis. cohort-A drove down overall p50 because it was ~half of requests and lower median. p99 improved because some long-tail large-token requests got temporarily routed to a fallback pool that happens to have better tail latency (maybe different GPU type or lower co-tenancy).

emily: okay. next question: what should the dashboard show so product understands this? current top-line percentiles are per-endpoint across all routing pools — hides cohort effects.

sam: we should add a small legend toggle: "split by routing_pool" and "split by client_tag". default stays aggregated but show an annotation when a routing policy change happens that moves >20% of traffic between pools.

devon: agree. also add sample count overlays on percentile charts (semi-transparent bars) so folks see weight skew. and when a policy change deploy occurs, capture a pre/post delta snapshot and pin it for 24h.

emily: can the console's rollout UI automatically attach the routing diff to the rollout changelog? that would help oncall/product.

jira-bot: Created ENG-1428: "dashboard: annotate endpoint percentiles with routing pool and client cohort deltas" — assignee: devex.

sam: minor API debate: our telemetry ingestion tags routing_pool at request time. for rollups we do weighted percentiles across tags. We need to ensure our percentile aggregation uses reservoir sampling consistent with small cohorts — otherwise p99 artifacts occur.

anjali: noted. we should also add a note in docs about how percentiles can be dominated by a high-volume low-latency cohort. recommendation: always inspect p99 in conjunction with token_bucket and routing_pool when making SLA claims.

emily: thanks all. action items: nora to attach cohort-level pct charts to the thread, devex (ENG-1428) will add UI toggle + annotation feature, platform (devon/sam) to check routing diff telemetry for correctness. I'll file a short postmortem blurb for product explaining metric artifact.

devon: quick check — I verified routing telemetry had no missing tags in that window. looks safe. :thumbsup:

emily: great. closing for now, will reopen if anomalies persist. :white_check_mark:
